caption: The drawing depicts a cylindrical drum with worn, faded edges painted in dark red and black around the rims. The main body of the drum features a large, prominently displayed eagle with brown wings spread open. The eagle holds arrows in its left talon and an olive branch in its right talon, and has a shield with red and white stripes and a blue field on its chest. Above the eagle, there is a pink and red ribbon or banner that curves in an arc, with white stars in a blue field surrounded by a ring of golden-yellow rays. The background of the drum’s main body is primarily a muted blue-green color, with hints of texture suggesting wood grain. Ropes are threaded vertically through metal loops on the sides of the drum, and the right side panel is decorated with rows of rounded brass or gold-colored tacks or studs forming a pattern. The artist’s name “ROSE CAMPBELL GERKE” is written in small letters beneath the drum on the right side. The rest of the background is plain, off-white or beige, with no additional objects or decorations.
title: Snare Drum
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
